dedupe_keys.name: opensn open source library for emulating leo satellite networks

description: OpenSN is an open-source library for emulating large low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks such as Starlink, developed at Beihang University in Beijing and presented at the Asia-Pacific Workshop on Networking in 2024 and in IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems in 2025. Unlike Mininet-based emulators such as LeoEM, it runs each satellite and ground station as a container, so that real distributed routing software can run on every node, and it scales horizontally across several machines. Compared with the container-based StarryNet it streamlines calls to the Docker interface and avoids unnecessary creation of virtual links, and it keeps user configuration apart from container network management through a key-value database. The authors report building mega-constellations five to ten times faster than StarryNet and updating link states two to four times faster than Mininet. The code includes a Go daemon, a Python SDK and topology configurators, a web console and container images for satellite routers and ground stations, relying on Docker, etcd and InfluxDB. Coverage: software for any constellation design. Format and access: GitHub repository, free under the MIT licence. Caveats: research software; orbital dynamics and radio links are simplified to link delays and states. Simulation uses: digital twins of satellite networks to test routing, failures and recovery, and integrated satellite and terrestrial network studies. Related records: Hypatia and StarPerf simulate LEO networks, and LeoEM emulates them with Mininet.
